id: P:Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun
summary: Anton Ferdinand Troyer von Aufkirchen und Thun (1775–1865) was an Indology scholar who studied at the Theresian Military Academy in 1787. He directed the Madras Military Institution (1807) and served as Secretary at Sanskrit College and University (1827–1835).
Anton Gerard van Hamel (1886–1945) was a linguist who studied at Barlaeus Gymnasium (~1898–1904). He held a post at Utrecht University from 1923 to 1945 and taught Jan Gonda.

Anton Kogan is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Russian State University for the Humanities from 1992 to 1997. In 2000, he became a Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Anton Scherer (1901–1981) worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his PhD at the University of Munich under Gustav Herbig, Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, and Ferdinand Sommer. He served as professor at the University of Würzburg (1948–1951) and Heidelberg University (1951–1969).

Anton Schiefner (1817–1879) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, the Peter the Great Museum, and the Roman Catholic Theological Academy.
Anton Walter Florus Gueth (1878–1957) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a docent at Taisho University in 1921 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 1922.
Anton Westermann (1806–1869) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as Mitdirektor from 1830 to 1865.

Anton Zigmund-Cerbu (1924–1964) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Bucharest, EPHE, INALCO, and under Jean Filliozat and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at the CNRS (1952) and Columbia University (1960).

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antoni Józef Śmieszek (1881–1943) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University, Berlin, Munich, and London. He held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (1922–1935) and the University of Warsaw (1934–1939).

Antoni Kałuski (1894–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Jagiellonian University (1912–1915) under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and Andrzej Gawroński, and also studied at the University of Chicago.

Antoni Muchliński (1808–1877) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial University of Vilna (~1824–1828) and held a post at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1866).

Antonie Rutgers (1805–1884) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Groningen and under Hendrik Arent Hamaker at Leiden University. He later served as extraordinary Professor of Hebrew at Leiden University from 1837 to 1875.

Antonino Forte (1940–2006) specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hōbōgirin (~1976–1989), the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1982–1999), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006).

Antonino Pagliaro (1898–1973) studied at Palermo, Florence, Heidelberg (under Christian Bartholomae), and Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer). A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and philosophy, he served as Professor of Glottology at Sapienza University of Rome (1936–1968).

Antonio Agostino Giorgi (1711–1797) was a scholar in Tibetology and Indology who studied under Giovanni Lorenzo Berti. In 1746, he became Professor of sacred writings at Sapienza University of Rome, and in 1752, he became librarian at Biblioteca Angelica.
Antonio Faiani (born 1859) was an Indology scholar who served as director of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio and Liceo Ariosto.
Antonio Marazzi (1845–1921) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia.

Antonio Rigopoulos (born 1962) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1987–1994) and became a Full Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 1999.

Antonio T. de Nicolás (1930–2022) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD from Fordham University (~1965–1968). He held a post at Stony Brook University from ~1969 to 1996 as professor emeritus of philosophy.
